about: Atlantis built into the stepped walls of the Monterey Canyon's deep south-western basin (tools/RUINS.md). The one table of where each building of the ruins stands, read by tools/build_atlantis_canyon.py (the model), by Bay (the ledges cut into the walls under them) and by Ruins (routes, kept-clear areas). World metres: x east, z south; depth in metres below the surface (40). The Ruins node stands at origin (x, z) and origin_depth; a building's own frame: its front is +Z, turned by heading (as Godot's rotation.y), y = 0 at its depth. A ledge: a rectangle (or a circle of radius) in the building's own frame, at its depth, `cut` (only lowers the floor to it), `fill` (only raises it) or `both` (levels it), blended out over `blend` metres, `above` metres over the building's depth if given (a fill behind a rock-cut front makes the cliff its rock is buried in). A terrace: the masonry block a building stands on, down to the floor. A facade: a rock-cut front (width, height, how far its rock runs back into the wall). A span: a bridge (half its length, its arch's radius, how far below the deck the arch springs). A stair: points (world x, depth, z), a flight between two of different depth, a landing between two at the same depth; each gets a ledge under its steps (its `mode`, as a building ledge's). After a change: godot -s res://tools/ruins_ground.gd, then the build, then tests/ruins_view.gd -- --check.
